items.title: My FOMO over The Duskbloods not coming to PC evaporated once I actually played it
items.summary: The vampire PvPvE game is a confusing mess that isn't going to be for everyone.

content.v: As a big Elden Ring person with an additional 600 hours in Nightreign, the FOMO of FromSoftware's next multiplayer experiment, The Duskbloods, being a Switch 2 exclusive was hitting me hard. That is, until I actually played it: I spent the majority of the closed network test held over the weekend confused about what the hell was going on, and even when I finally learned, I wasn't particularly impressed.

To be fair, the network test wasn't built to make a great first impression. It was limited to one map, six playable characters, no build customization, solo queue only, and seemed to only have a portion of its intro tutorial. I also experienced borderline unplayable input lag from the Switch 2's docked and handheld modes, which meant I was fighting the basic controls for longer than I'd like.

Assuming the final game will have all of that fixed and more, I might end up liking The Duskbloods in the end. Elden Ring Nightreign didn't click for me for close to 20 hours, and when it did, I dug it so much I spent the first half of this year playing it daily, even climbing to the highest level of its ranked mode. The Duskbloods might reveal itself to be a masterfully created vampire multiplayer game, but as it stands right now I think it's an aimless mess of intriguing systems that don't cohere into anything worth PC gamers buying a $500 ( for now ) console for.

What does impress me is how bizarre The Duskbloods is as a videogame in 2026. At times it felt like playing a PlayStation 2 game I brought home from Blockbuster with an offbeat multiplayer mode someone cooked up with before battle royales and hero shooters codified a framework for how it's done. Tutorial popups will tell you things like, "To obtain Virtue visit Sites of Ritual to pledge yourself on the Eve of the Third Moon before the final Bestowal." That's the kind of needlessly opaque but deliciously evocative language I love to see in a FromSoft game, but it also does absolutely nothing to prepare you for what it's like to actually play it.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/WHqWwLVsVnuMwYnGAL7Yof.png

The simplest way I can describe The Duskbloods is by using MOBA words. It's a game about killing creeps to level up and collect Virtue points as you prepare for the final PvP team fight (or free-for-all in solos) at the end of every match. Enemy players are there to gank you or be ganked by you as you race to become the strongest combatant in the lobby. Otherwise, collecting Virtue is your entire goal from the moment you and seven other players drop into the map and the first round begins. The rest of the game's systems are there to disrupt you on your quest to farm as much Virtue as possible so you don't get kicked, or culled, from the match early.

Even though I expected the PvP aspect of The Duskbloods to be the worst part as someone who avoids it in FromSoft's other games, it's actually so meaningless for the majority of a match that I almost wish there was more reason to hunt down players, but it's huge risk with little reward. Dying to other players doesn't do anything but set you back on your Virtue farm. It's more lucrative to play it like you're speedrunning a normal Souls game with opportunities to PvP every now and then if you want.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CHuor6yXaDLxCFEtBcAZ5g.png

On paper, the Nightreign player in me should eat that up. This is a game where everyone can triple jump and air dash like it's nothing. Over the course of my matches, however, I never fought anything that required more than your usual attack-and-dodge approach. Most monsters die in a few hits and the bosses ping-pong between players while everyone spams attacks into them until they die. I can't tell which ones, if any, are supposed to be fodder like in a MOBA or challenging foes that reward you for memorizing their moves. At times, the hardest fight was with my eyelids, as I farmed the same mincemeat enemies over and over again. The routine is only occasionally broken by another player engaging a boss that lets everyone join under a temporary truce to help fight it. My hope is that the final game has more of these moments that rely on having a handful of players participating.

The Duskbloods desperately needs more reasons to care about its cast of certified freaks and their unique skills that aren't purely PvP-focused. I love that I can turn it into a third-person shooter as Sniper Layla and press a button to make a gatling gun burst out of her chest, but standing still as you one-shot weak enemies gets stale real quick. Trang Lanh's invisibility skill is largely useless against monsters who all have big attacks that'll hit you anyway, which just reduces her into a weaker melee character. Even everyone's favorite walking submarine, Zork, plays like your typical heavy-armored Souls character until other players show up and you actually have a reason to rocket yourself into them (AKA "Zorking it" ).
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/D42hoyQHGmdXLZQXYfwzJg.png

Recruiting enemies as allies by yelling at them until they surrender is also great, as are the unique Kin you can have by your side. I found a shirtless man named Baritone who stood by me and sang to give me a defense buff and a small snake girl inexplicably named "Gargoyle" who healed me. You can level these weirdos up and have them tank tougher monsters for you, which ends up being pretty important as you get deeper into a match. The Kin are Elden Ring's Spirit Ash summons if they were smarter and permanent—a really fun idea that I hope future character kits can build around. Unfortunately, the Kin feel ill-equipped for the speed of PvP fights, even sometimes sabotaging you by ruining a sneaky ambush by sprinting straight into battle.

Even with its problems, I am fascinated by FromSoft's irresistible premise: a bunch of vampires from different eras and factions fighting on the eve of an apocalypse to give themselves up to a giant moon dripping with blood. I would like to know why there is a steampunk airship in the sky and why one of the bosses looks like Bloodborne's Lady Maria riding on a headless horse. There are echoes of other FromSoft games imbued into the world, but so far it's only enough for director Hidetaka Miyazaki to remind us that better games exist.

I used to be a believer that The Duskbloods would eventually make its way to the PC, but recent comments from Miyazaki seem to imply Nintendo's involvement was so pivotal to the project that I wouldn't be surprised if the exclusivity is indefinite. We've got another Bloodborne on our hands, apparently.

So with us computer-havers being denied the chance to play The Duskbloods with better framerates and no paid subscription, maybe we're not missing much. Its best ideas fall flat in a game that is mostly about farming enemies like you're on a quest in an MMO from 10 years ago. Nothing about it grabbed me and I'm worried it might end up being the first FromSoft game that I simply skip.

content.v: 近日光荣特库摩公布《 三国志14 威力加强传承版》假想剧本“英杰会聚”内容和画面，秦始皇嬴政、项羽、刘邦、李世民、朱元璋跨越时代同台争霸。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260825/1787609233_499666_jpg_r.jpg
通关全部教程关卡即可解锁该特殊剧本。其中首次登场的明太祖朱元璋势力，初始拥有资金20000、兵粮65000、士兵30000，难度三星。专属政策还原 历史 典故“高筑墙，广积粮，缓称王”，带来独特的内政发展玩法，配套还有徐达、常遇春、刘伯温、李善长、马皇后等明代文臣武将。除历代帝王外，梁山好汉武松也作为新增古武将加入游戏。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260825/1787609233_854704_jpg_r.jpg
本作不只是新增假想剧本，还带来大量系统层面升级：全新军情侦察系统，派遣武将侦查获取情报，情报可以强化离间、伪报、外交计谋，情报过期还会出现虚假信息。新增“功劳‑方策”养成链，武将通过作战积累功劳实现能力成长，再消耗主张点解锁势力科技树。AI逻辑优化，同盟配合、武将布阵策略更强。游戏加入总计190个历史事件、100处中华名胜与配套诗文，中文文本全面润色打磨。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260825/1787609233_641847_jpg_r.jpg
《 三国 志14 威力加强传承版》将于9月10日发售，登陆PC(Steam)、PS4、PS5和Switch。Steam分为完整版套装288元，老玩家升级包128元两个版本。不少玩家十分期待跨时代帝王对决的脑洞剧本，希望推演不同朝代霸主的胜负。也有部分玩家讨论定位，认为传承版属于整合全部DLC的终极决定版，已有原版威力加强版的老玩家需要权衡是否重复购入。

items.summary: EA被沙特财团收购后，背上了200亿美元巨额债务。有业内人士分析，为缓解债务压力，EA有可能处置一大批长期搁置的经典游戏IP。曾在EA任职近十年、现任Newzoo市场情报总监的Emmanuel Rosier在采访中表示，

content.v: EA被沙特财团收购后，背上了200亿美元巨额债务。有业内人士分析，为缓解债务压力，EA有可能处置一大批长期搁置的经典游戏IP。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260825/1787609111_767523_jpg_r.jpg
曾在EA任职近十年、现任Newzoo市场情报总监的Emmanuel Rosier在采访中表示，EA库存中囤积大量长年没有新作规划的沉睡IP，典型代表有CRPG开山之作《创世纪（Ultima）》、太空射击名作《银河飞将》，除此之外还有《模拟城市》《火爆狂飙》《地下城守护者》《孢子》等一大批老系列。
他提出两种可能性：EA会选择直接将部分IP对外出售，或是外包交给外部工作室接手开发，甚至有可能改编为手游项目。
分析指出受巨额债务压力影响，EA需要削减开支，出售闲置IP可以快速回笼资金。当下就连BioWare推进《质量效应5》都阻力重重，很难说服管理层批准老IP的3A级别重启项目。与其继续封存，转手或者外包是更现实的出路。
不少EA经典IP目前甚至没有在主流PC商店上架，玩家只能依靠民间补丁与非正规渠道体验，大量宝贵的游戏遗产被束之高阁。不过本次仅为行业人士的分析推测，EA官方尚未公布任何出售IP计划。
该消息在网上引发讨论，不少玩家期待部分老IP能流转到更适合的开发商手中。也有玩家担忧经典系列转手后，会被改造为手游、氪金产品，彻底毁掉原作内核。

items.title: 《黄昏血族》网络封闭测试比《艾尔登法环：黑夜君临》还要火

content.v: 看来粉丝们非常渴望了解From Software的Switch 2独占游戏《黄昏血族》，因为该游戏的一位制作人透露，这款游戏的试玩注册人数比《艾尔登法环：黑夜君临》还要高。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260825/1787608866_935480.webp
在由日本游戏杂志《Fami通》主持的直播节目中，From Software市场部总监北尾泰大（Yasuhiro Kitao）表示，《黄昏血族》试玩版的申请数量超过了该开发商之前的多人游戏实验《艾尔登法环：黑夜君临》。
北尾说：“我们真的很惊讶。”
考虑到《艾尔登法环：黑夜君临》之前是在PS5和 Xbox Series X|S上开启的游玩测试，而《黄昏血族》仅在 Switch 2上测试，因此后者的更受欢迎确实更值得关注。Switch 2是一款相对较新的主机，上市至今仅一年左右，这意味着其用户群体远小于其他两款主机。
表面上看这令人惊讶，但或许其中蕴含着一些逻辑。
《艾尔登法环：黑夜君临》最终销量超过500万份，其DLC就在不到一周的时间内售出200万份。这款游戏的成功证明了From Software能够制作出极具乐趣、以多人游戏为核心的类魂游戏，这或许也为《黄昏血族》的开发带来了更多关注。
此外，在封闭网络测试之前，关于《黄昏血族》的信息几乎一片空白，这或许也助长了玩家的好奇心，促使他们踊跃报名参加。虽然玩家们知道这是一款多人游戏，但《黄昏血族》的具体架构、可玩职业以及游戏机制都还是个谜。而由From Software传奇总监宫崎英高亲自操刀，无疑也为《暮血军团》增添了不少光彩。
如此庞大的试玩申请数量对《黄昏血族》来说是个好兆头，即便网络测试初期由于服务器和连接问题导致From Software取消了第一场测试。

content.v: CDPR宣布，《巫师4》将于2028年发售，登陆PS5、 Xbox Series X/S和PC平台。CD Projekt RED联席CEO Michal Nowakowski在视频中公布了这一消息。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260825/1787606838_247946.jpg
CDPR表示，今年的科隆展他们将展示《巫师3》新DLC“旧时曲”的完整预览，但不会展示《巫师4》，因为他们还没有准备好。《巫师4》将是他们迄今规模最大、最大胆、最具野心的一款游戏，同时确认2028年发售。
值得注意的是，官方表示希望大家能每天准时收看这次的科隆展特别节目，可能会有1-2个惊喜。
希里：
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20260825/1787606838_813963.jpg
“我想邀请大家观看8月26日的开幕之夜直播，并莅临科隆游戏展现场。今年我们将推出重磅内容，带来非常特别的《巫师3：狂猎》 ——旧时曲。我们将展示这款扩展包的诸多精彩内容，包括其黑暗故事的片段以及即将带来的全新体验。如果您有时间，欢迎莅临科隆游戏展，我们在8号展厅设有大型展位，我们的团队将为您带来《旧时曲》的首次完整预览。此外，请务必收看每天的RED特别直播。我们或许还会分享一两个惊喜。”
“当然， 《巫师》的世界远不止于此。我们CD Projekt Red总部的团队正在紧锣密鼓地打造一个全新的传奇故事，由希里领衔主演。我们拥有超过500名才华横溢的开发者，致力于为您打造真正非凡的作品。《巫师4》拥有庞大而沉浸式的开放世界、紧张刺激的动作游戏体验，以及一个深刻动人的故事，我们希望它能长久地留在您的记忆中。简而言之，这是我们迄今为止规模最大、最具魄力、也最具雄心的作品。”

“我知道你们都迫不及待地想知道《巫师4》何时发售。我们一直听到你们问这个问题。虽然我们不会在本次展会上展示《巫师4》，目前也无法透露确切的发售日期，但我可以告诉你们，《巫师4》的目标是在2028年发售。我知道这需要等待一段时间，你们肯定也想早点玩到，但请耐心等待，让开发团队慢慢打磨。一切等待都是值得的。在此之前，《巫师》系列还有更多精彩内容即将推出，包括将于2027年发售的《旧时曲》。而且，请放心，科隆游戏展也在我们的未来计划之中。我们路上见！”

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Devs Vow to Update Captain Price After Botched Haircut Goes Viral
items.summary: Publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward have promised to update Captain Price's hair in Call of Duty:

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-4-captain-price-hair-1787605087848.png
Publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward have promised to update Captain Price's hair in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 after images of his botched haircut went viral.

As last weekend's closed beta dredged up conversations revolving around its time-to-kill (TTK) speeds and problematic spawn placements, other fans aimed at Captain Price and his barber. It's mostly thanks to a few images that have circulated across social media, with fans pointing out that, maybe, Modern Warfare 4's version of the classic character should invest in some hair gel.

He looks…unwell, at least when compared to past versions of Captain Price. Whether he's chasing down Vladimir Makarov or walking you through a training course, Price is known to have a full head of hair and a beard that could make even Ghost blush. The one from Modern Warfare 4, however, has neither of those things, and according to many, he hardly looks like the Task Force 141 leader fans have come to know. Activision and Infinity Ward say that's not their intention, but there's also a good reason why only some Call of Duty fans are encountering this choppy imposter.
bro.... https://t.co/JxOTxMTny3 pic.twitter.com/WQEHOTgdEU
that ain't captain Price that's lieutenant Cost https://t.co/gtAFT18NhF
That ain’t price that’s amount

While the Captain Price making the rounds online does appear to be real, he'll only look this way in Modern Warfare 4 if users tune their devices to the lowest possible settings. Some had expected this to be the case, as reports of the botched haircut seemed to mostly be few and far between.

Still, the developers and Activision and Infinity Ward are going to do their best to give the Call of Duty fan-favorite Operator the head of hair he deserves. The studio community teams X/Twitter account replied to a few of the more popular posts, promising it would be addressed "in a future update."
"Captain Price's hair does not appear correctly when viewing his character model at the lowest level of detail," a tab in the "Known Issues" column from the Modern Warfare 4 Trello says.

Hello! We're aware of an issue with Price's hair not appearing correctly when viewed at the lowest level of detail. The team will be addressing it in a future update. Ultimately this will not be an issue if players meet our recommended specs. Details: https://t.co/uozRRLS3W5
What in the 1050 TI is this? Whoever took that screenshot got the game at ultra low, ultra performance, 11% resolution. pic.twitter.com/Pq3A5BdzFt

What exactly that update entails remains to be seen, but it's far from the only thing on the team's list. Also noted in the Known Issues category are dropped framerates when cooking lethal weapons, hitches for PC players during their first multiplayer matches, a stuck loadout screen bug, and more. TTK is another issue the team is looking into , as are those spawns.

So, if you find yourself dissatisfied with the Modern Warfare 4 beta, you might want to take another crack at it when the open beta launches this weekend . You can learn more about everything it comes with, including its single-player mission, here .

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has a release date of October 23, 2026, for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X | S. For more, you can read about how it will allow players to remove masks for some of its Operators . You can also check out IGN's interview with the team to learn about Infinity Ward's approach to matchmaking, the beta, and more.
Image credit: X user @Runhob.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

items.title: Canceled Iron Man Game Footage From Just Cause and Mad Max Developer Leaks Online
items.summary: Alleged footage from Avalanche Studios' canceled Iron Man game has surfaced online.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2022/09/20/iron-man-ea-motive-1663686372718.jpg
Alleged footage from Avalanche Studios' canceled Iron Man game has surfaced online.

In the early 2010s, Just Cause and Mad Max developer Avalanche Studios was working on an Iron Man game . The project was never officially announced to the public, but Avalanche Studios co-founder Christofer Sundberg confirmed its development and cancellation during an interview in 2022. Now, gameplay for that title has popped up online via Reddit , reportedly sourced through a PS3 developer kit.

The gameplay is extremely unfinished, but it shows Iron Man flying around in a large environment, fighting jets and attacking various facilities. One of the more in-depth videos appears to be an unfinished E3 demo which shows Iron Man in hand-to-hand combat with soldiers, using a heavy, Arkham-esque style of combat. Of course, he also boasts his repulsors, missiles, and other gadgets to help take down all of his targets.

One of the more standout features is that the environments would've been at least semi-destructible. Iron Man can throw foes through walls, slice them apart in order to make shortcuts for himself, and tear up buildings around him. Beyond that, the build isn't far along enough to really distinguish itself much from SEGA's MCU Iron Man games. It certainly shows promise, though. Given how fun the studio's Mad Max game is and the sandbox gameplay of the Just Cause series, Avalanche probably would've made a killer Iron Man game.

There is still some hope, however. EA Motive is currently developing a new Iron Man game , though details on the project are extremely scarce. The project entered development in 2022, but there haven't been any updates since then. EA was also working on a Black Panther game, which was canceled last year . However, Iron Man has remained in development, despite fears that it will suffer the same fate. Given it has been four years since the announcement, hopefully we are close to hearing some news on the title.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Latest GTA 6 leak confirms full dong
items.summary: It's perfectly natural.

content.v: I'll be the first to admit that I have my reservations about enigmatic cryptopeddler / self-appointed anticorporate folk hero / world's most humdrum most wanted suspect Cyberleek. But I can't say their repeated leaks haven't done us all the service of answering our most burning GTA 6 questions—questions like, "If I play GTA 6, how often should I expect to confront someone who's just straight up hanging hog?"
Thanks to Cyberleek's latest illicit gameplay drop, the answer for that particular question is: Quite often, if you're frequenting one particular spot in the state of Leonida.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8mUxgWFStriutEKpPtdB2k.jpg

If you're not picking up what I'm putting down, the title of the most recent GTA 6 leak should help you with that sticky wicket: It's called "nudist_town.mp4," and it consists of the player surveying the uncensored denizens of an in-game nudist retreat—some of whom are, justifiably, unenthusiastic about being creeped on from mere feet away by a dude in work jeans with a pair of binoculars.

And when I say uncensored, I mean uncensored. We won't share the leaked video here for legal reasons, but if you seek it out yourself—it's not hard to find—you should expect to see the full spectrum of human bits and bodies matching every description except "clothed."

It's not exactly a Hot Coffee scenario, however. There's some close-proximity twerking and gyrating happening, but aside from the bared genitalia, there's really not much explicit activity going on as GTA 6 protagonist Jason takes in the scenery. There's just… a bunch of naked people standing around. I guess nudists do just as much aimless loitering as the rest of us.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Ee4X5pRorHpBkdRRgbxwmF.jpg

Perhaps there's a lesson there. But if there is, Cyberleek doesn't seem very receptive: The video ends after they start shooting everyone because one of the nudists got mad at them for creeping too hard. Or at least, they tried to shoot everyone, and in the process dumped most of a magazine into some deck chairs. It seems Cyberleek shoots as well as they drive.

As with their previous GTA 6 leaks, nudist_town.mp4 features the expected QR code directing viewers to the cybercurrency scheme animating this whole operation. But it sounds like Cyberleek has graduated to the "making demands" stage of internet notoriety: The text watermark plastered on-screen throughout the footage says "to show support at least 10 gamers need to show up dressed as leeks in front of Take-Two / Rockstar offices holding game discs during working hours."

We'll see how that goes, I guess. Considering a YouTuber was arrested mere months ago for trespassing on the Rockstar North office premises, my expert advice would be to be normal instead. But hey, in the meantime, full dong confirmed.

items.title: This Legend of Zelda Brain Teaser Recreates One of the Best Side Quests From Tears of the Kingdom

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/zelda-puzzle-1787601281002.png

Tears of the Kingdom was an excellent game. IGN even went as far as to call it a perfect 10 out of 10 when it first came out on the Switch. And while the boss battles, gameplay, and massive open world definitely contributed to its masterpiece status, it was all of the little side quests that brought it all together for me.

One particular quest that made TotK's Ultrahand abilities shine was helping Addison put up President Hudson signs throughout Hyrule. Now, in 2026, that very quest has been brought into the real world with a brain teaser puzzle.

You have a lot less material to work with than many of the sign puzzles in the actual game, so you can't just start sticking massive boards to the bottom of the sign to keep it upright. Instead, you need to find a very specific solution.

Along with the sign (made of metal) and Addison himself, you have four metal logs to work with. The product page calls it "worthy of a level 6" challenge, so I wouldn't expect the solution to be straightforward.

Once you actually complete the brain teaser, you'll have a little metal figure of Addison and his President Hudson sign you can display on your desk or shelf. The Bepuzzled brand has several other Legend of Zelda-themed puzzles you can check out as well, including the Hyrule Crest and a Master Sword.
More Legend of Zelda Gifts to Check Out

If you (or a Zelda fan you know) are in the market for cool Legend of Zelda merch, there's certainly no shortage of things you can buy. In addition to the game itself, there's a number of Legend of Zelda books and manga worthy of being added to your shelf. We've curated some of our favorites gifts for fans of the franchise , but there's a lot more where that came from.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. content.v: It sounds like fans were eager to learn everything they could about From Software's The Duskbloods , as one of the game's producers has revealed the Switch 2 exclusive saw higher playtest sign-ups compared to Elden Ring Nightreign .

Speaking during a livestream hosted by Japanese gaming publication Famitsu (and translated by GamesRadar+ ), From Software producer Yasuhiro Kitao stated the number of applications for The Duskbloods playtest eclipsed that of the developer's previous multiplayer experiment.
"We were really surprised," Kitao said.

Given that Elden Ring Nightreign's playtest was available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S (the full game was also available on PC and last-gen consoles) the fact that The Duskbloods received more interest on Switch 2 sounds like it should be impossible. The Switch 2 is also a relatively new console, having only been available for around a year, meaning its user base is much smaller compared to that of the other two consoles.

While it is surprising on the surface, perhaps there is some logic to be deciphered here. Elden Ring Nightreign went on to sell more than 5 million copies , with its DLC alone selling 2 million copies in under a week . The game's popularity and success proved From Software could make a wildly fun, multiplayer-focused souls-like, perhaps generating more interest for The Duskbloods.

It also probably helped that there was almost no information known about The Duskbloods prior to the closed network test, encouraging players who wanted to learn more to sign up. While players knew it was multiplayer in nature, the exact structure of The Duskbloods, its playable classes, and its mechanics were all a mystery. The Duskbloods being helmed by legendary From Software director Hidetaka Miyazaki also doesn't hurt.

Such a large number of playtest applications bodes well for The Duskbloods, even if the network test got off to a rough start with server and connectivity issues that saw From Software cancel its first session. The test also served as the world's first introduction to Zork , one of the game's playable characters that has already become a bit of a meme.

GameSpot's Jake Dekker came away impressed during his hands-on The Duskbloods preview , saying he'd "never played anything like it" and "couldn't wait to play more." The Duskbloods is still slated to release sometime this year but does not currently have a release date.

items.title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Is Way Ahead Of Black Ops 7 Already By One Metric
items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is nearing 400,000 copies sold on Steam already, and that's well ahead of where

content.v: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is nearing 400,000 copies sold on Steam already, and that's well ahead of where last year's Black Ops 7 stood at launch on Valve's platform. This is according to Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics , who added that pre-sales on Steam alone work out to around $21 million in revenue.
Elliott said Black Ops 7 managed to hit around 200,000 copies pre-sold on Steam by launch. Modern Warfare 4 has doubled that, and with two months still to go before release.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/CODMW4_df79f1.jpg?w=636

MW4's beta put up big numbers on Steam during its early-access period, reaching a peak of more than 115,000 concurrent users . Black Ops 7, meanwhile, peaked at about 100,000 concurrent users on Steam, even after it went live for everyone outside of a beta weekend, according to ChalieIntel.

MW4 performing better than Black Ops 7 by some metrics already is not a total surprise, as last year's game was a commercial disappointment. In fact, its sales ranking in the US was the lowest for the series since 2008 .

The next MW4 beta is coming up this weekend, running August 28-September 1. This will be an open beta, so anyone on any platform can play without needing to preorder. Additionally, this beta will extend to Nintendo Switch 2.
MW4 is expected to have stronger outright sales overall in part on PC because it is not included with PC Game Pass like Black Ops 7 was.
Impact on console sales

Elliott also observed that MW4 could help improve sales of PS5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles. MW4 is the first entry in the series since 2013's Call of Duty: Ghosts to skip PS4 and Xbox One, so the launch of MW4, combined with the current-gen-only GTA 6, will "for sure nudge the last-gen holdouts," Elliott said.

The newest consoles are more expensive than ever today, thanks to a variety of factors, including tariffs, AI, and the capitalistic demands to always make more money . As such, anyone buying a new console to play MW4 or GTA 6 who hasn't kept up with the news is in for a shock at the register or online checkout. For its part, Microsoft is encouraging people to buy a used console or use a Buy Now, Pay Later service to help fund the cost of an expensive new console.
MW4 launches on October 23, while GTA 6 arrives at long last on November 19.

Konami has announced an official line of Metal Gear Solid cat merchandise that'll be available exclusively at CatCon 2026, to mark the release of Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 . We swear we're not making this up, but Konami says that it will have a booth--again, at a cat convention--where it will sell the novelty items for two days in October.

According to Konami, attendees can purchase cat-scratch boxes modeled after the iconic boxes of Big Boss and Old Snake, as well as plushie pet toys and cat collars inspired by Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker and Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots. The goodies will also be sold through OKS Gear Shop for those two days. You can stick to digital cardboard boxes in classic Metal Gear Solid games in case you don't want to take that risk, as Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 launches for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch consoles on August 27. items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Adds New Dynamic Cosmetic Options for Certain Characters Like Ghost
items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is adding more options for how your operators appear in-game.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/05/28/cod4image1-1779986564142.jpg
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is adding more options for how your operators appear in-game.

The recently released Modern Warfare 4 beta has given players their first look at a ton of features, maps, and other content that will be available in the final game. Some of these things were heavily advertised before launch, such as the fluidity of movement and a new system that randomly generates gun builds for you.

One feature that was kept under wraps, however, allows players to equip different cosmetic items on the fly in-game. Ghost, for instance, can remove his mask (which comically reveals another cloth mask underneath) and put it back on. Valeria can equip a hockey mask. And Captain Price can smoke a cigar, which will appear on-screen in first-person at all times unless you take it out.
You Can Remove Ghost's Mask in Modern Warfare 4 using the NEW 'Operator Variant' Feature in the Emote Wheel: pic.twitter.com/ABJma6tvsy
this is the best MW4 mastercraft the cigar actually stays in ur mouth until you respawn lol pic.twitter.com/sFWQUrV02k

It's a fun touch and one that will almost certainly be taken advantage of in premium skins. As of right now, we're not sure what skins to expect in MW4, but Call of Duty has promised to keep things more grounded after fan backlash to previous games. Specifically, they said there will be "no Lady Gaga. No Omni-Man. No Teletubbies. No SpongeBob."

The fan reception on Modern Warfare 4's beta has been fairly divisive so far. Some fear that the game is a bit too fast, especially for having relatively small maps. The time-to-kill is extremely rapid, but Infinity Ward has addressed much of this feedback from fans so far. The studio has released patches for the beta addressing TTK, spawns, and is also looking to make improvements to the gunsmith system for launch.

IGN spoke with some of MW4's multiplayer leads last week ahead of the beta, and they made it clear this playtest is essential in helping shape the final game. "To me, this beta feels like the start of the conversation with the public, you know what I mean? We're excited to basically put that out there and we'll see what happens next. We want to just keep talking and keep learning and trying to find out what we can do better," said Jackie Reynolds, Modern Warfare 4's multiplayer design lead.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Red Dead Redemption 2 Is Getting A Mexico Expansion Soon, But Not From Rockstar
items.summary: Red Dead Redemption 2 never received official story DLC, but one modder is doing the work developer Rockstar n

content.v: Red Dead Redemption 2 never received official story DLC, but one modder is doing the work developer Rockstar never did with an ambitious Mexico mod that will further connect the prequel to the events of the original Red Dead Redemption.

It's called Nuevo Paraiso--The Forgotten Frontier, and a new trailer highlights what fans can expect from the project. Alongside restoring and recreating Mexican locations from the original Red Dead Redemption, the mod also adds new settlements, gang hideouts, treasure hunts, minigames, bounty-hunter missions, random encounters, and more.

The mod even features a new protagonist for the series, Sadie Adler. She's a prominent character from Red Dead Redemption 2 who mentions moving to South America. That means it's not too much of a stretch to assume she traveled through Mexico on the way there, giving the mod a convenient hero that doesn't conflict with the game's existing story.
Though playing as Sadie will be "reccommended" for narrative reasons, players can choose to experience the mod as franchise faces Arthur Morgan or John Marston as well.

This isn't mod author Roxis724's first rodeo. They are responsible for a number of different Red Dead Redemption 2 mods, including an earlier Mexico expansion that served as the starting point for Nuevo Paraiso. However, over the last few years, the scope and ambition of the mod looks to have grown considerably.

In an update about the mod's development from January, Roxis724 stated the development team was working to not only make the mod look great, but to feel "real" and reflect the "oppression, despair, and social tension" of the time period. The goal is to provide an immersive experience that sets the stage not only for the events of the original Red Dead Redemption but real Mexican history.

"More than a journey across the border, The Forgotten Frontier expands the world of Red Dead Redemption 2 while providing a glimpse into the social and political tensions that would soon erupt into the Mexican Revolution of 1911, giving players a deeper understanding of the events that shaped Mexico and its people," the trailer's description reads.

Red Dead Redemption fans won't have to wait much longer to experience Mexico, as Nuevo Paraiso--The Forgotten Frontier is slated to release September 16. It will be available to download for free on PC through Nexus Mods.

Rockstar, of course, has had its hands full developing Grand Theft Auto 6 in recent years. The game's November 19 release date is inching closer with an official deep-dive reveal slated for August 27. In the meantime, a string of high-profile and ongoing GTA 6 leaks has given fans their best look at the game in action, even as Rockstar works to find the person responsible .

items.title: Why A Nintendo Direct Is Likely To Happen Next Month
items.summary: There's something about September when it comes to Nintendo Direct events . The company behind Mario, Link, an

content.v: There's something about September when it comes to Nintendo Direct events . The company behind Mario, Link, and Donkey Kong has held special livestreams during that month in nine out of the past 10 years. The only exception is 2024, but even then, there was a Nintendo Direct on August 27 (an Indie World Showcase alongside Partner Showcase).

With that sort of history, a Nintendo Direct seems very likely to occur next month. For starters, there are two big elephants in the room: release dates for The Duskbloods and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake . Both are slated to come out this year, so it's about time for more specifics on these hotly anticipated titles.

In addition, Nintendo also likes to pull back the curtain on the following year's lineup during September Direct events. For instance, last year's presentation saw the company reveal Mario Tennis Fever , Yoshi and the Mysterious Book , and Pokemon Pokopia . These are all Switch 2 exclusives that arrived in the first half of 2026. Before that, in the September 2023 Direct, Nintendo unveiled Princess Peach: Showtime (which launched in March 2024) and the remaster of Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door (which arrived in May 2024).
Here is a breakdown of dates for Nintendo Directs in September over the past decade:

Early 2027 still seems fairly open for Switch 2, meaning Nintendo needs to fill out the calendar. Xenoblade Genesis could possibly be on the way during that timeframe, or maybe we'll be surprised with Pokemon Winds and Waves . As noted above, it's more than possible that totally new games are revealed, too.

Nothing is official yet, obviously, but looking at the past paints a clearer path for when Nintendo Directs happen. With that, it's safe to assume a new Direct is coming sooner than later. And there is plenty to talk about for Switch 2 this holiday season and into next year.

items.title: Pokémon Collector Poses as Buyer to Recover $4,000 Worth of Stolen Cards in 'Vigilante' Sting Operation
items.summary: Canadian collector Emilio Kihien took matters into his own hands after police said they “couldn’t do much” to

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/pokemon-card-collector-poses-as-buyer-to-recover-stolen-cards-1787592495584.jpg
Canadian collector Emilio Kihien took matters into his own hands after police said they “couldn’t do much” to help him recover $4,000 worth of stolen Pokémon cards.

Kihien was conducting what he thought was a standard sale for a few highly-graded, officially-encapsulated Pokémon trading cards at his home in Coquitlam when the buyers handed him $4,000 in phony bills, snatched the goods, and ran. Kihien gave chase, even hanging onto the side of the thieves’ getaway car before falling onto the road, suffering bruising and a painful bout of road rash as a result.

His next step was to contact police — but he says authorities told him they “couldn’t do much” to help him recover his stolen property. According to Kihien, one officer even told him it’d be better to try and catch the culprits himself.

“The police response — they really didn’t seem like they were gonna help me that much. One of the officers literally said, ‘If it was me, I’d probably just try to set them up myself,’" he told local outlet CTV News .
A few days later, one of Kihien’s buddies came across a listing for the stolen cards online. The thieves even used the exact same images Kihien had included in his original posting.
“I’m just thinking, you know what, these guys can’t be the most intelligent of people,” he remarked.

Acting quickly, Kihien and his friends posed as interested buyers, and set up an exchange at the Metropolis at Metrotown in Burnaby on August 13, where they detained the alleged thieves until police arrived. Reports state one adult and one juvenile were detained, who could face criminal charges including theft.

Kihien recorded the entire ordeal on his smart glasses, showing himself and his friends blocking the suspects from leaving the Barnaby mall. And while their sting operation proved successful, police are urging future victims of theft against such measures.

“Vigilantism can only cause problems,” Royal Canadian Mounted Police Corporal Mike Kalanj said. “No one knows who has weapons. Even as the victim, if you show up and you harm someone, now you’re looking at charges, as well.”

The stolen cards went mostly unharmed, though one case was cracked in the altercations. The haul included three 2023 Pokémon Mew EN Special Illustration Rare EX cards (for Blastoise, Venusaur, and Charizard), graded a PSA 10 — meaning the agency could find no flaws with them , whatsoever.

This is the latest Pokémon TCG crime to make headlines after a pair of thieves in Britain were locked up for making off with £71,000 ($95,000) worth of stock after their getaway van broke down in July.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

items.title: I turned car friction off in GTA 5. Help
items.summary: I have died 400 times in the last 20 seconds. I have accelerated Samsara's Wheel to the speed of light.

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .
Sometimes happiness isn't a new thing, you know? Sometimes it's about wringing novelty out of what you've already got, finding a new perspective on old things and enjoying them to their fullest.

It is in this spirit that I have not installed a new mod in GTA 5 this week, but used an old one to set a constant and unstoppable momentum on every NPC car in the game. Also, I turned friction off. Specifically, I used the Enhanced Native Trainer that I installed in order to spawn the anti-air truck from the very first mod I put into GTA 5 . Turns out there's a whole bunch of stuff in here!

It's really quite wonderful. Los Santos has gone from a humdrum facsimile of Los Angeles to an unforeseeable carnival of movement. Vehicles, newly loosed from their obligations to the ground, now waft lazily through the air. Standing on the balcony of Franklin's home, you can watch them gyrate on the skyline like lightning bugs.
Sometimes you try to cross the road and get vaporised by a transit van travelling at a fraction of the speed of the light. That does also happen sometimes.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2WFHPzgxFjhwsywfp8UxJf.gif

It's great fun, though. But I have a confession: originally, I set every car to travel at maximum speed , a setting which was great laughs but made the game functionally unplayable. I have since set them to around 15. I don't know 15 of what, but the setting is 15. The maximum setting was 100, so it's quite a bit lower. It just means all the same chaos that was happening at max speed still happens, just in a way that you stand a hope in hell of navigating.
Welcome to Los Santos, the most airborne little city on Earth.

items.title: The Long Game: The 4 Best Crops to Invest in Early in Stardew Valley

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/20/1-header-1787254744336.jpg

We’re starting a new series at IGN called The Long Game, where we focus on things you can invest in early in new or popular games that will pay off in the long run. We’re starting this series with Stardew Valley, which celebrated its 10-year anniversary this year and is one of the most successful indie games of all time.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/20/2-general-tips-1787254553380.jpg

If you’ve never played Stardew Valley before, it’s a farming and life sim where you leave your job at a soulless corporation to manage a farm left to you by your deceased grandfather. The farm has seen better days, so it’s up to you to restore it to its former glory. That means clearing the land, tilling the soil, planting and watering seeds, and upgrading your home and equipment to gather items more efficiently.

As you might expect, those upgrades cost money. There are several ways to make that money, like fishing and mining, but harvesting and selling crops is the best way to keep a steady stream of income. And there are four specific plants that are the most cost-effective options at your disposal.

But before we get into those specific plants, we have some general farming tips for you to be aware of. First, you normally need to water your seeds every day for them to properly grow. But if it’s a rainy day, you can skip that step and let Mother Nature handle it for you. Check the TV in your farmhouse to see the weather report, which will tell you when rain is coming and help you plan ahead.

We also highly recommend crafting scarecrows and sprinklers as soon as you’re able to. Birds can sometimes swoop in and eat the crops you worked hard to grow, but scarecrows prevent that. And sprinklers will automatically water the area around them, allowing you to skip hand watering even when it’s not raining.

And finally, the seasons change every 28 days in Stardew Valley and almost every crop is seasonal, meaning they will wither when a new season begins. Since the game starts in spring, those are the crops we’ll be focusing on to gain wealth as early as possible and set you up for success.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/20/3-parsnips-1787254573168.jpg
Parsnips

This starter crop will be the foundation on which you build the rest of your farming journey. You get your first few seeds for free, and after that you can buy more for 20 gold each at Pierre’s General Store. They grow in four days, then can be sold back to Pierre for 35 gold each. Getting back nearly double what you paid for them can really add up in the long run, and it’s a good idea to keep a handful of parsnips planted throughout your first spring.

Because they have such a short growth time, if you stagger them with other crops, you’ll have consistent money coming in. But of course, this is just the start. Once you’ve made a little cash, you can incorporate the next crop into the mix.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/20/4-potatoes-1787254615524.jpg
Potatoes

You don’t need to boil ’em, mash ’em, or stick ’em in a stew to make potatoes worthwhile. They cost 50 gold at Pierre’s and can be sold back for 80, so there’s obviously more upfront cost but the profit is double that of parsnips. They also take six days to sprout, which is why you shouldn’t move on to exclusively farming these, just add them to the rotation.

While that’s all well and good, the true value of potatoes comes from the possibility of getting a double harvest. Every time you pull a potato from the ground, it has a 20% chance of having a surprise second potato with it. That requires some luck, but it’s a nice boost to your profits when it happens. And its sell price can help you move on to farming the next crop on the list.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/20/5-cauliflower-1787254655069.jpg
Cauliflowers

A cauliflower seed costs 80 gold, the same amount you get back for selling a harvested potato. And you can sell cauliflower for a whopping 175 gold, giving it one of the biggest profit margins of any spring crop. The downside is that it takes 12 days to grow, which is nearly half the season. So you have to pay attention to the timing of when you plant them.

But if you’re patient and use the funds from harvesting potatoes to grow cauliflower, then you’re basically starting with a 50 gold investment into potato seeds and getting back 175 gold in the end. Plus, you’ll get a letter from Jodi requesting a fresh cauliflower, which she’ll give you 250 gold for. So it pays to be prepared ahead of time.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/20/6-strawberries-1787254693867.jpg
Strawberries

Our last recommendation is the most involved and requires a different approach to get the most out of it, but it’s the poster child for an early investment having a huge payoff down the line. You’ll first be able to buy strawberries during the Egg Festival on the 13th day of spring, where they cost 100 gold each. That’s expensive, but trust us, it’s worth it.

Make sure you have enough money to buy at least a handful, then plant most of the seeds immediately. Notice that we said most, not all. You should save some, and you’ll see why in a minute. Strawberries take eight days to grow, but once they mature, they’ll regrow a new strawberry in four days. And there’s a chance of you harvesting an extra strawberry, though the odds are much lower than potatoes. They sell for 120 apiece, and if you plant them ASAP, you’ll be able to harvest them twice before the first spring ends, meaning you can get 240 gold back for the 100 you spent on the original seed.

That’s a nice profit, but you’ll really start making bank once spring comes back around. In the second spring, on Day 1 you can plant the strawberry seeds you saved. With the ability to now take advantage of the full season, if you use a Speed-Gro fertilizer when you initially plant it, you can harvest strawberries six times. That’s a total of 720 gold made from the original 100 gold purchase, with any double harvests you luck into adding even more profit.

And that’s our list. If you’re hopping into Stardew Valley for the first time, was this helpful? Or if you’re a seasoned vet, was there something we missed? Let us know in the comments, and for more in The Long Game series, stay tuned to IGN.

items.title: Former Rockstar dev says the GTA 6 leaks are a 'nothing burger': 'There won't be much damage'
items.summary: The Cyberleek debacle is no Hot Coffee.

others.title: Former Rockstar Dev Calls GTA 6 Leaks 'A Nothing Burger,' Insists Hot Coffee Was Much, Much Worse

content.v: Rockstar is currently enduring one of its most embarrassing PR episodes in recent memory: With just days remaining before its Netflix-exclusive Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay reveal, the developer is on the hunt for the cryptopeddler whose 11 leaks of illicit GTA 6 footage over six days seem to imply ongoing access to a playable game build .

While Rockstar and its parent company Take-Two are almost certainly at DEFCON 1 over the historic shitshow, former Rockstar developer Obbe Vermeij says the GTA 6 leaks will ultimately prove to be, well, kind of whatever.
"Calm down everybody," Vermeij said in a post on X over the weekend. "The leaks are a nothing burger."

According to Vermeij, who spent nearly 14 years at Rockstar North as a technical director on every GTA release from GTA 3 in 2001 to GTA 4's Ballad of Gay Tony expansion in 2010, the recent GTA 6 leaks will likely constitute little more than "a tiny blip" for a game whose sales lifespan, if GTA 5 is any indication, is expected to span more than a decade.

"All that has happened is that some footage has escaped. Slightly ahead of the Netflix thing next week," Vermeij said. "90% of future players don't spend their time on the internet looking for video snippets. They don't have the time and don't want spoilers."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/QhR9yvN9u4shoXm448uV9D.jpg
The Cyberleek situation, Vermeij says, is "far less consequential" when compared to the biggest "nightmare" he witnessed during his Rockstar tenure: the infamous Hot Coffee incident.

In 2005, the discovery that GTA: San Andreas had shipped with code for a sex minigame that could be enabled through unofficial modification earned the game an Adult Only re-rating from the ESRB. In the ensuing PR firestorm, retailers pulled San Andreas from store shelves until an updated version could be issued, leading to an estimated $50 million revenue loss in 2005 and a $20 million class action settlement in 2009.
Measured against that level of brand damage, Vermeij said in a response to another X user that he figures "there won't be much damage if any" from the GTA 6 leaks.

Even if Cyberleek does something drastic like leak GTA 6's ending, Vermeij—who himself once ran afoul of his former employer by publishing a short-lived blog detailing his GTA dev days—doesn't think it would move the needle much.
"That would suck," he said , "but people will still play it."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/kkNtsnEsZiTdgmuFTn4pJ6.jpg

items.title: Hideo Kojima Says He’s Aware Of His Mortality As He Celebrates 63rd Birthday
items.summary: Game designer Hideo Kojima celebrates his 63rd birthday today, August 24, and he does not plan to pack it up a

content.v: Game designer Hideo Kojima celebrates his 63rd birthday today, August 24, and he does not plan to pack it up anytime soon.
Posting on social media , Kojima said he is aware he will not live forever--in fact he already knows how he wants to die --so he is being particularly thoughtful about how he spends his time.

"As I get older, the things I 'have to do' and the things I 'want to do' continue to increase. At the same time, the time I 'have to do them' continues to decrease," he said. "I constantly need to reassess how I use my time and how I live my life. That said, once you’ve taken something on, you can’t simply put it down and walk away."

Kojima also pointed out that 2026 marks his 40th anniversary of making games, having begun his professional career in 1986. Additionally, 2026 represents the 10th anniversary of Kojima Productions, the studio he founded after leaving Konami. At the latter, he ran an internal unit also called Kojima Productions.

Also in his post, Kojima said he wants to "remain focused on creating games," even though he is receiving "various opportunities and offers" to do other things. He didn't elaborate as to what these might be, but it was previously reported that Kojima was asked if he wanted to direct the Death Stranding movie before he opted to sit out and let Michael Sarnoski direct.
Kojima has a number of projects currently in the works, including the espionage game Physint and the horror game OD .
Kojima Productions seemingly updated Death Stranding 2's night sky scene to honor Kojima's birthday.
What's more, Kojima's staff got him a pretty boss cake--check it out below, along with a photo of Kojima and his friend Geoff Keighley.

This is a preorder deal that ends August 27, the day the game releases — or when Fanatical runs out of codes. In other words, time’s running out, so grab it soon.
Save 23% Off Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 2 (Steam)

As the “Vol. 2” in the title suggests, this is the second collection of Metal Gear Solid games. The first came out in 2023 and was very well received — as it should be, since it included the first three games in the trilogy, all of which are stone-cold classics. This new collection contains the following games:

The most notable inclusion here is Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots . This collection represents the first time that game has ever been available on a platform besides PlayStation 3 (and how many of us still have a PS3 connected to a TV?). It’s a phenomenal game that’s unlike any other and carries the MGS story to its conclusion (MGS 5 is a prequel). Upon its 2008 release, IGN gave MGS4 a 10/10 in our review .

Extra Content

Metal Gear Solid 4

items.title: Control Resonant Made Me Feel Foolish For Ever Doubting It — IGN First
items.summary: I played two brand new Control Resonant missions and feel foolish for ever doubting it. Our final preview:

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/13/ign-first-controlresonant-6-thefinalpreview-blogroll-1786627528052.jpg

I first played Control Resonant back in June, having made my way through the same couple of hours as my colleague, Mitchell Saltzman, detailed in IGN’s first preview . Much like him, I had a great time getting to grips with the series’ newfound melee systems, hacking and slashing away at the Hiss threats that have broken out into the sequel’s open Manhattan. But I’ll admit that introduction did leave me a little wary of whether the dial may have been turned a little too much to the action side of things, and wondering if its open-world playground was merely there to serve as a place to grind XP and hone combat skills. As the studio steps further into the world of the action RPG, is it necessary to tread ground that won’t click with me in the same way Remedy’s previous games did?

So, I stepped into my exclusive two-hour-long demo of Control Resonant hoping to see more of what I love so much about Remedy’s output — unrivalled world-building, consistently surprising level design, and simply being shown things I haven’t seen before. Thankfully, I was not disappointed.

Do not fear, there’s plenty of weirdness here. Even the fast travel points are mysteriously placed doors that conjure looping snapshots of the surrounding scene within their frames when opened. This is a New York of Remedy’s design, one that takes familiar art deco architecture and bends it into the studio’s own image. Yes, there are flashes of other science fiction worlds here — one note I read even playfully references Inception and its folding city — but the Finnish developer firmly puts its singular stamp down wherever it can.

I felt it most keenly in the first of two brand new missions I got to play, which took me deep into the Big Apple’s subway system in search of the Reach ability, Resonant’s grapple hook equivalent. The Metro Vault is one of many “dungeons” where traversal abilities are learned, but they also push the story forward in interesting ways — often showing glimpses into protagonist Dylan’s relationship with his sister, Jesse, and their intertwining tales that have led to this moment. They’re a prime example of Remedy’s well-honed ability to layer each of its levels with both narrative and gameplay purpose, all while putting things on your TV that you’ve not quite seen before.

Here, in the middle of Metro Madness, trains hurtle across the screen from every direction, showing no respect for the laws of physics. Dylan is able to shift the gravitational pull of the tunnels at will; With the press of a button, he can make the ceiling his floor in order to better navigate the screeching obstacles that rattle along each perilous passage. It’s a neat bit of puzzle platforming that makes you question each and every leap of faith. When faced with a gaping drop into the unknown, in most games the wrong call would be to fall all the way down. But Control Resonant doesn’t like to play by the rules, with the void acting as the critical path. Curiosity is rewarded in both its linear and open areas.

These winding corridors are also full of Mold enemies, a returning faction you can read all about in my deep dive into Resonant’s enemies. They pose a different threat to the much more common Hiss, proving much harder to directly damage due to their armored casings. But while you need to find and exploit their weakness, I appreciate that there’s no single solution to effectively taking down an enemy. While the fire-sparking Heat Wave and Heat Aura abilities can melt through the Mold’s armour plating, if you haven’t equipped either, you can do exactly what I did and use your shape-shifting weapon, The Aberrant, to conjure a giant hammer and bash their hardened outer layer off, then shift to a blade form to slice up their fungal insides. This flexible approach to combat means minimal time is spent in menus crafting builds, and more time toe-to-toe with the threats you’ll be taking down with them.

Speaking of which, the second mission I was dropped into featured the Central Resonant, one of the sequel’s big bosses. But before I could battle it, I first had to find its lair. Working out the building it called home was simple enough — a towering smokestack stretching improbably high into the sky revealed a factory as such a place — but getting in there and finding its exact location within those walls was another challenge altogether. To do so, I had to fend off a few bothersome Hiss, which I did so using the satisfying tactic of bulldozing into larger enemies with my trusty rock shield, which builds up enough of their stun meter to allow me to deliver a slick finisher with The Aberrant's dual-blade form.

Over the course of my few hours with Resonant, I can’t say I ever felt anything approaching boredom with its combat, which consistently delivers a feel-good power trip in each encounter. Key to this is Remedy’s decision to kill off all minor grunts in an area after you’ve defeated the larger enemies within a horde. It helps keep the game’s momentum going, without bogging you down in battles that could otherwise outstay their welcome.

Once the streets were clear, I could get on with solving the puzzle needed in order to open the factory’s doors. This involved stabbing a nearby electrical power source with Dylan’s blade, which can hold a charge for a limited time, and scuttling as quickly as I could to an unpowered cube in need of energy. I’d previously engaged with a more complex version of this puzzle, which had me transporting power across roads and rooftops between multiple generators, which put my traversal skills to the test. It’s encouraging to see that Control Resonant’s open world challenges won’t be limited solely to combat, but also test your mental muscles, too.

A prime example of this was when I came into contact with an Altered Item — everyday objects that have developed paranatural properties in the Control Universe. In this case, it was a Polaroid camera that disappeared with a flash and snap every time I approached it. In order to get close to it, I needed to find an alternative way into the room and sneak up on it from behind. Doing so made it vanish again, but this time kicking off a whole new side questline that seemed to insinuate I’d be meeting this camera many more times on my travels across New York. It’s these sorts of strange sojourns that allayed any fears I had that Remedy was going too action-heavy in this sequel. Rest assured, there’s still plenty of that weirdness and puzzle-solving that the original featured so heavily.

But back to the mission at hand. Upon entering the factory, I ventured down into its depths only to be met with a series of steaming hot pipes blocking my progress. So, into its intertwining tunnels I went in search of a way to clear a path. This led to a cluster of intense battles, side paths full of upgrade materials, and plenty of lore pertaining to horrors that took place here – horrors that resulted in a sixty-foot-tall magma monster living in the factory’s bowels. It’s the backstory I found here that made this whole area come to life for me, as some of that trademark Remedy dark humour pierced through an otherwise desperate situation.

items.title: Blood Dungeon review
items.summary: The creators of Nidhogg and Wheel World tackle the bullet heaven genre, but can't transcend its inherent weakn

content.v: What is it? Nidhogg creators take on the 'bullet heaven' or Survivors-like roguelite Release date August 26, 2026 Expect to pay TBC Developer Messhof Publisher Messhof Reviewed on RTX 3060 (laptop), Ryzen 5 5600H, 16GB RAM Steam Deck Officially "unknown", but works great Link Steam

Blood Dungeon adheres rigidly to the autoshooter or ' bullet heaven ' format: it's about moving around a scrolling arena auto-gushing projectiles that turn a steadily increasing horde of enemies into XP. Every level up grants a choice between two or three randomised perks or improvements, steadily turning the player into a blur of pulsating DMG-emitting fireworks. Rounds are usually over in less than ten minutes.

I loved Vampire Survivors but then I got over it. I've never been gripped by any of the clones. But Blood Dungeon has some appealing bullet points going for it: it transforms the commonly top-down autoshooter into a sidescrolling platformer. At a glance, it looks more like Spelunky than it does Brotato or Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor.

The presentation is more appealing than your average bullet heaven fare too: Blood Dungeon is the work of Nidhogg studio Messhof and their distinctively globular 2D art style is a perfect fit for precision-oriented action. Animations in particular are often brilliant, and the music—which its creator Matthew Hoey aptly describes as dungeon drum 'n' bass—is simultaneously madcap and hypnotic.

There's no denying Blood Dungeon is a sleek, well-wrought take on this modern subgenre. It's probably among the best examples of it. But as the hours I spent with it wore on it started to feel exquisitely meaningless. I was reminded why I dropped Vampire Survivors.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/WZihw3huE4Dh9M4CYRZHBK.jpg
Blood Packed

Blood Dungeon starts like all roguelites: vainly. I am Gun Man, a man with a piddling machinegun which shoots every 1.21 seconds. Thanks to the blood left by my fallen enemies, within a minute I've upgraded it to shoot twice rather than once, and then, thirty seconds later, I've acquired a sword that rotates around my body, shredding bats as I roam the lurid halls. By the time I die there are four double-sized swords surrounding me, my gun issues five bullets per round virtually non-stop, and the halls have turned into impenetrable walls of monster flesh.
Every map has a fixed layout but the locations of items and keys are, for the most part—but not entirely—randomised.

Five hours later I've unlocked a handful of other characters and all six of the maps. I've upgraded my health, my jump height, my damage output, the amount of weapons I can equip per run, and my repertoire of powerful upgrades has expanded dramatically. If I'm lucky my character will be lost among an overwhelming array of erupting, tantruming firepower by the eighth minute.

My favourite weapon for achieving this is easily the bouncing ball, which can demolish most of the game's first bosses within seconds if I focus on upgrading it. I also love the turrets and the laser, though the shotgun whose spread can be increased from three to upwards of 13 shots is pretty fun too.

I also like most of the characters, except the unwieldy flying mosquito (I'll admit it's a skill issue). They all throb with panic, which well they should. My overall favourite is probably Skinja, who cartwheels around the maps at a blinding pace while issuing volleys of the aforementioned shotgun pellets. I also liked the Baby, whose low health is well-compensated by a revolver that one-shots most early round enemies. There's also Hypnomancer, who loads out with gas which, naturally, he farts from his arse.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/SupSWTyG5sDnkGLbAdZpCK.jpg

But it's the sidelong perspective that appeals to me most, even though all maps stick to common survivor archetypes: there's the X-axis corridor map, the Y-axis pit map, and other gimmicks like the map with a lot of water, and the map you have to mine through. Importantly, every map has a fixed layout but the locations of items and keys are, for the most part—but not entirely—randomised.

Most maps also loop back on themselves, so the genre's sense of constant, hysterical forward momentum is complemented by a newfound focus on map knowledge: knowing where to reliably find health and explosives is the difference between beating the area's third and final boss or dying for the umpteenth time to its second. If I spend the less frantic opening minutes unlocking as many doors as possible, it'll make the final minutes when there's barely a safe place to stand much easier.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/mNiSUs9VwwbcFvVYvrkrCK.jpg
Slot Your Throat

But Blood Dungeon does inevitably feel like a grind. The opening hours are an enticing onslaught of rewards and unlocks, but by the ten hour mark, with my fist deep in its basket of candy, the basket is ripped away and my nose pressed to the grindstone. It lays bare the disappointing truth that the game itself can't withstand the absence of its rewards.

Still, Blood Dungeon feels superb to play which is essential for an arcade game but oddly, kinda rare for a Survivors-like. I guess most Survivors-likes don't need to feel good because the genre usually amounts to little more than a slot machine simulator. It fast-tracks RPG character progress so that dopamine hits come thick and fast in units of seconds rather than hours. Then, in the final five seconds or less, assuming the RNG hasn't been so kind as to make me unstoppable, it steals everything away and invites me to start again.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/sTPwzXncE673W4qvNXaaEK.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PvwTZiASfoGfuxiMH93UEK.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HhD6peLRp2BzDUCxYUcxAK.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GYeqUWQCbo9BAR5BTGY8AK.jpg

I can get better and better at moving around in Blood Dungeon but if the RNG doesn't favour me I'm still stuffed. Being at the mercy of chance is baked into its design, of course, but there is a big unambiguous line between the story-generating unpredictability of a Nethack or Spelunky and the more-ish, non-nutritive unpredictability of a lottery.

And that's ultimately what Blood Dungeon and its ilk feel like to me, once I've put the controller down and walked away from their exquisitely compulsive loops and dazzling visual noise. It's addictive, and that's the only reason I keep playing it. It gets easier as I play, but that's not because I've improved much: it's overwhelmingly attributable to the wider array of weapons, charms and spells I have at my disposal at hour fifty versus hour one.

Still, Messhof pulls its own Survivors-like off with flair and applies a thin layer of skill reward. I enjoyed the time I spent playing it. But now that I've put it down, I never want to think about it again.
